primary_question: Does the funding + price-dislocation feature set improve out-of-sample forecasts of a signed-jump / semivariance-asymmetry TAIL event (next-24h jump component above an expanding, train-only high quantile per coin) beyond a realized-volatility-only baseline on the broad ironflow_bulk panel, clearing a frozen materiality floor?

design.target: jump event y_t = 1 if J_{t+1..t+24} > q_t
design.jump_definition: J = sign(RS+ - RS-) * (RV - BV), RV = sum of squared 1h log returns over next 24h, BV = bipower variation, RS+/RS- = realized semivariance of positive/negative returns
design.quantile_q_t: expanding, train-only per-coin high quantile (0.95) of trailing signed-jump magnitude |J|, shifted by 1 (no future information)
design.baseline: RV-only (persistence / HAR-style trailing log-RV lags) logistic
design.candidate: RV-only + signed funding_rate + abs(funding_rate) + mark/index premium + mark/EMA24 distance

materiality_definition: candidate relative Brier (or log-loss) improvement over the RV-only baseline must exceed 0.02 (2%); verdict is symmetric PROMOTED / NOT_SUPPORTED

verdict_rule.PROMOTED: materiality_met is True AND candidate beats baseline on Brier (Holm-adjusted)
verdict_rule.NOT_SUPPORTED: materiality floor not met (valid, publishable negative result)

universe: coins present in candles_1h AND funding AND open_interest (intersection), with sufficient trailing history for train-only quantile
frozen_inputs_note: ironflow_bulk 18 monthly parquet per dataset; sha256-asserted; read-only; bounds 2025-05 .. 2026-10
